hero.title: Navigate Montreal's winter, one better step at a time.
hero.subtitle: Compare the shortest walk with a winter-aware alternative. See confirmed closures, unverified reports and the gaps in our data — each one clearly labelled.

scene.description: Illustration: a low-poly winter street lined with triplexes and exterior staircases, snowbanks along the sidewalk, streetlights, a pedestrian, and a highlighted walking path under falling snow.
scene.illustrative: Illustrative scene — not a real street or live conditions.

items.title: Two routes, side by side
items.body: See the shortest path next to a winter-aware alternative, with distance, time and how much of each route has no condition data.

items.title: Evidence you can read
items.body: Every datum carries a label: confirmed, unverified report, model estimate, unknown, or simulated. Unknown is never shown as safe.

items.title: Accessible by design
items.body: Step-free routing excludes anything not verified as step-free. Every route comes with a text list of directions, not just a map.

preview.title: What the planner shows
preview.body: A full-screen map with closure and report overlays, a comparison card for both routes, and step-by-step directions you can read without the map.
preview.label: Product preview — illustration, not live data

steps.title: Choose your start and end
steps.body: Click the map, type coordinates, or share your location — only if you choose to.

steps.title: Compare two routes
steps.body: We compute a shortest route and a winter-aware route using open data from the city, OpenStreetMap and Environment and Climate Change Canada.

steps.title: Read why
steps.body: Each route explains what it avoids and where data is missing, so you can decide for yourself.

privacy.title: Privacy and data limits
points: Your location is used only if you allow it, and only for the route you ask for. We don't track you or store your route history.
311 requests are reports, not confirmed obstacles. Snow-loading plans don't tell us whether a sidewalk is cleared.
Coverage is limited to the McGill / Downtown pilot area. Outside it, we show nothing rather than guess.

partners.title: Who we're building pilots for
partners.intro: These are the settings we're designing for. They are not current customers.

items.title: Universities
items.body: Help students and staff move between buildings in winter with transparent route information.

items.title: Campuses & hospitals
items.body: Step-free options and clear information about known closures near entrances.

items.title: Municipalities
items.body: Aggregated, privacy-preserving insight into where pedestrians run into winter barriers.

items.title: Property managers
items.body: Understand reported issues around your properties without collecting personal data.

items.q: Does WinterPath tell me a sidewalk is cleared or safe?
items.a: No. We only show a condition as confirmed when an official source says so. Everything else is labelled as a report, an estimate, or unknown.
Only in the McGill / Downtown Montréal pilot area for now. Requests outside it return a clear "outside pilot area" message.
Not directly. Any risk model predicts the chance of winter-related 311 reports, which is a reporting proxy — not physical ice. It stays disabled until it passes an evaluation.
No. There are no accounts and no route history.
We design for WCAG 2.2 AA and test with automated tools, but we haven't completed a formal audit, so we don't claim compliance.

ctaBand.title: Ready to try it?
ctaBand.body: Plan a walk in the pilot area and compare both routes.
